podcast.title: Alleged Murder-for-Hire Offer from Courtney Love (1993)
podcast.body: Elden Hoke, known as Elduchet, claimed in the April 1996 edition of High Times Magazine that Courtney Love offered him $50,000 in December 1993 to kill her husband, Kurt Cobain. He quoted her as saying, "I need you to blow my old man's head off. I'll give you $50,000 to blow his effing head off." "Elduchet claimed that in December 1993, Courtney Love offered him $50,000 to kill her husband."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Documentary Appearance and Reiteration of Claim (Post-1994)
podcast.body: Elden Hoke repeated his claim about Courtney Love's murder-for-hire offer in the Nick Broomfield documentary "Kurt and Courtney." In the documentary, he explicitly stated, "She offered me $50,000 to whack Kurt Cobain." "This is a claim that Elduchet repeated in the Nick Brumfield documentary Kurt and Courtney."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lie Detector Test Results (1996)
podcast.body: On March 6, 1996, Elden Hoke took a lie detector test for a national TV show, administered by Dr. Edward Gelb. Dr. Gelb concluded there was a 0.01% chance Hoke was lying, indicating a 99.99% chance that Hoke genuinely believed he was telling the complete truth regarding Courtney Love's alleged offer. "Dr. Gelb concluded that there was a 0.01% chance that Elden Hoek was lying."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mysterious Death by Train (1997)
podcast.body: Elden Hoke died in the early morning hours of April 19, 1997, when he was decapitated after being hit by a train while returning home from a gig. His official obituary stated his death was "the result of being hit by a train in a state of alcoholic intoxication," a circumstance some found "a little weird." "In the early morning hours of April 19, 1997, he was decapitated when he was hit by a train coming home from a gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Allegations Against Kurt Ylov
podcast.body: Edom Hock, an artist who knew both Kurt Cobain and Kurt Ylov (being closer to Ylov and not very successful), claimed in an interview months after Cobain's death that Kurt Ylov had offered him $50,000 to kill Kurt Cobain, which he refused. "un artista que se llamaba Edom Hock, que eran conocidos de los dos, pero era más amigo del Córnilov y no tenía mucho éxito, en un entrevista una vez dijeros, pocos meses que Córnilov la había ofrecido 50.000 dólares por matar a Córkovend y te lo había rechazado."

srcs.episode: El secreto de La muerte de Kurt Cobain

podcast.title: Mysterious Death
podcast.body: Three days after making the allegations against Kurt Ylov, Edom Hock was found dead under suspicious circumstances. Police were unable to clarify the motive for his death, as he had no apparent issues with money, drugs, or conflicts with others, and his death seemed to lack any apparent justification. "A los tres días, ese hombre aparecía muerto, me estrellaste en constancias, sin que la policía pudiese aclarar el motivo por el que se podría haber asesinado, no tenía problema de dinero, no tenía problema de drogando, tenía problema de enfrentamiento, es con nadie, realmente apareció muerto sin ninguna justificación aparente."

xref.title: Corroborated Meeting Location (1993)
xref.body: Elden Hoke's claim about Courtney Love offering him money was partially corroborated by the owner of a record store called Rockshop on Wilcox Avenue in Los Angeles. Hoke stated Courtney pulled up in a limousine outside the store and exchanged car keys, a detail the owner confirmed. "The owner of the store corroborates Elduchet's story."

xref.title: Elden Hoke's Allegations of Murder-for-Hire (December 1993)
xref.body: Elden Hoke (Eldu-Cher), frontman of the punk band The Mentors, publicly claimed in a 1996 High Times interview and a 1998 documentary that Courtney Love offered him $50,000 in December 1993 to kill Kurt Cobain. Hoke stated she said, "I need you to blow my old man's head off." He recounted an exchange outside a Los Angeles record store, corroborated by the owner, and said Courtney later called for him in March 1994. Although Hoke passed a lie detector test, his claims remain unverified and are often dismissed due to his unreliable narrator status. "Eldu-Cher claimed that in December 1993, Courtney offered him $50,000 to kill her husband."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Connection to Courtney Love (Post-1994)
xref.body: The Mentors, an extreme LA punk band, became tangentially involved in the Kurt Cobain death investigation through two of their members. Guitarist Eric Carlson (Sikki Wifebeater) dated Carolyn Rue, who helped Courtney Love found Hole, and it was through this connection that Courtney met singer Elden Hoke (Elduchet). "Carolyn Rue, helped Courtney Love found Hull. She once went out with the guitarist of the mentors, a dude by the name of Eric Carlson, who worked under the name Sikki Wifebeater."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Elden Hoke's Side Project (Post-1994)
xref.body: This band was a side project formed by Elden Hoke (Elduchet), the singer of The Mentors. The band's name itself reflects Hoke's direct accusations against Courtney Love regarding Kurt Cobain's death. "Elle Ducet had a side project to the mentors. The man was called Courtney Killed Kurt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Follow-Up Attempt for Hit (1994)
xref.body: Elden Hoke further claimed that in March 1994, Courtney Love called the Rockshop, looking to give him "the word to go ahead" with the alleged murder plot. However, Hoke was on tour at the time and missed the call, preventing them from connecting again. "Courtney until March 1994 when she allegedly called the store looking to give Elle the word to go ahead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Motive for Alleged Murder (Post-1994)
xref.body: Elden Hoke theorized that Courtney Love had Kurt Cobain "whacked" because he was preparing to divorce her on adultery charges. Hoke believed she needed him dead quickly to secure financial benefits. "I think Kurt was getting ready to divorce her for adultery charges. The theory goes, she had to have him whacked right away so she could get the money."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "Kings of Sleeze" Self-Description
xref.body: The Mentors, an extreme punk band from Los Angeles, proudly referred to themselves as the "Kings of Sleeze," a moniker that reflected their provocative and controversial image. This self-proclaimed title was frequently associated with their frontman, Elden Hoke (Eldu-Cher). "They proudly refer to themselves as the Kings of Sleeves."
